clue.text: Last document by Shakespeare (abridged)

definitions.meaning: a person's last ... and testament is the final document they sign
William Shakespeare's first name cut short gives his familiar nickname

explanation.surface: A final manuscript by the Bard, published in shortened form.
explanation.definitionFit: A testament disposing of property after death is the last document, and the Bard's first name shortened is his familiar form.

clue.text: Solo time that's involved in Sunday school songs

indicators.note: being involved in something means being wrapped up inside it, so these pieces go within the outer pair

parts.note: Han Solo is the Star Wars smuggler
that is, in Latin id est, abbreviates to i.e.

explanation.surface: A solo spot is woven into the hymns sung at Sunday school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solo' looks like a musical term but is Han Solo; 'that's' is read as 'that is', i.e.
explanation.definitionFit: Sea shanties are traditional work songs sung by sailors.

clue.text: Sportsman asks Russian cheats: "Help expose ringleaders"

indicators.note: the leaders of each word are their opening letters, so the first letter of every word here is taken

explanation.surface: An athlete calls on Russian dopers to help reveal the people running the cheating.
explanation.walkthrough: The leaders of the words from 'asks' to 'expose' spell ARCHE; the indicator 'ringleaders' then contributes its own leading R, a self-referential touch.
explanation.definitionFit: An archer competes in archery, an Olympic sport, so is a kind of sportsman.

clue.text: Gardner's head bears fine American plant

parts.note: F is the pencil-grading abbreviation for fine
Ava Gardner was the Hollywood film star
bean is slang for the head

explanation.surface: A gardener's chief grows a fine plant from America, with Gardner nearly a misspelling of gardener.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gardner' tempts as gardener but is the actress Ava Gardner; 'bears' just shows her name carrying F in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Fava bean is the usual American name for the broad bean plant.

clue.text: About 6, we retire to study

parts.note: re means about or concerning
VI is 6 in Roman numerals

indicators.note: to retire is to go back, so the word we is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Around six o'clock we withdraw to the study.
explanation.walkthrough: '6' looks like a cross-reference to 6 down but is just the Roman numeral VI.
explanation.definitionFit: To review material is to go over it carefully, which is to study it.

clue.text: Boy heads?

definitions.meaning: the heads are the toilets on a ship

explanation.definitionFit: It is a common boy's name, and in American slang a toilet, which sailors call the heads.

clue.text: Cliff diver: "I've taken off backwards on wobbly chair"

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece placed on another comes after it
something wobbly is unsteady and out of shape, so the letters of chair are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the remaining letters are read from right to left
letters taken off are removed from the word diver

parts.note: taken as written
the letters of I've, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A cliff diver announces he has leapt backwards from a rickety chair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cliff diver' reads as one thing, but 'Cliff' is the definition, pointing to the singer Cliff Richard; 'taken off' and 'backwards' work on 'diver' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Cliff Richard is the British pop singer, so his first name points to his surname.

clue.text: '70s prog rock band books castle

parts.note: Camel were an English progressive rock band of the 1970s
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A seventies progressive rock group reserves a castle for a gig.
explanation.definitionFit: In Arthurian legend this is King Arthur's castle and court.

clue.text: Sugar, part of a balanced diet?

indicators.note: only a part of the phrase a balanced is used, a run of its letters

explanation.surface: Is sugar allowed in a balanced diet?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sugar' looks like food but is the businessman Alan Sugar, of the British version of The Apprentice.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord Sugar, the British tycoon, has this as his first name.

clue.text: European husband, one in Paris again, swims across river

parts.note: un is French for one

indicators.note: the shuffled letters lie across the river letter, enclosing it
letters that swim move about freely, so again is rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A European husband goes back to Paris and swims across a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swims' rearranges AGAIN into GAIAN... read as GA-IAN around R, giving GARIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hungarian is a person from Hungary, a country in Europe.

clue.text: Complaint? Fans want Spoonerism

indicators.note: a Spoonerism swaps the opening sounds of two words, named after the Reverend Spooner

parts.note: to fan air is to blow it
to want something is to need it

explanation.surface: A grumble from supporters who are demanding a Spoonerism.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening sounds of BLOWS NEED gives 'nose bleed'.
explanation.definitionFit: A medical complaint is an ailment, and bleeding from the nostrils is a minor one.

clue.text: Day cleaning out interior of antechamber gets one in order

parts.note: Fri is the abbreviation for Friday

indicators.note: clearing out the inside of the word antechamber leaves only its two outer letters

explanation.surface: A day spent clearing an antechamber leaves someone in good order.
explanation.definitionFit: A friar is a member of a religious order such as the Franciscans.

clue.text: Special style of loud hot rock

parts.note: f, forte, is the musical marking for loud
lava is molten rock from a volcano

explanation.surface: Loud hard rock music has its own distinctive style.
explanation.definitionFit: Flava is slang, from hip-hop, for a distinctive individual style or character.

clue.text: Former football manager of Villa and Forest?

definitions.meaning: Tim ... managed Aston Villa, an English Premier League club, in 2015
the Nottinghamshire woodland of the Robin Hood legend

explanation.surface: Who once managed both Aston Villa and Nottingham Forest?
explanation.walkthrough: Villa and Forest look like two football clubs, Aston Villa and Nottingham Forest; only Villa belongs to the manager, and Forest is the woodland.
explanation.definitionFit: Tim Sherwood managed Aston Villa, and the Nottinghamshire woodland is Robin Hood's home.

clue.text: Some atmosphere at wizard's postcode?

definitions.meaning: a layer of gas in the upper atmosphere, made of three-atom oxygen
the Wizard of Oz's address would be in district Oz, number one, like a UK postcode

explanation.surface: A wizard's home address has a bit of atmosphere about it.
explanation.definitionFit: This form of oxygen makes up a layer of the upper air, and as Oz 1 it would be a postcode for the Land of Oz.

clue.text: To restrict opening of safe, secure with key

parts.note: to cap something is to put a limit on it

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: to lock something is to secure it

explanation.surface: To limit access to a safe, fasten it with a key.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the keyboard key that switches on capital letters.

clue.text: Boy: "Wonder about nickel, boron and gold?"

indicators.note: turned about, the chemical symbols are read in reverse order

parts.note: Ni is the chemical symbol for nickel
B is the chemical symbol for boron
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: Batman's sidekick, the Boy Wonder, marvels at some chemical elements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boy' with 'Wonder' recalls Batman's sidekick, the Boy Wonder; 'Wonder' only adds to that picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Robin is a boy's first name, and Batman's young partner is called the Boy Wonder.

clue.text: One takes notes, one plays notes

definitions.meaning: a person or device that writes down or records what is said
a woodwind instrument, the simple fipple flute played in schools

explanation.definitionFit: A clerk who keeps records writes notes, and the woodwind instrument plays musical notes.

clue.text: Gas inhaled by heavy-duty criminal

indicators.note: something inhaled is taken inside, so these letters go into the other piece

parts.note: HD is the standard abbreviation for heavy-duty
oxygen gas is O2, a molecule of two O atoms

explanation.surface: A tough villain breathes in some gas.
explanation.definitionFit: Hood, short for hoodlum, is slang for a gangster or thug.

clue.text: Professional hitter from Edinburgh dismissed — bowled out

indicators.note: out here means out of shape or disordered, so the remaining letters of the city are rearranged
a batsman bowled is dismissed, sent away, so that letter is removed from the city name

parts.note: taken as written
b is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for bowled

explanation.surface: A cricket batsman from Edinburgh is dismissed, bowled out.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is cricket, but 'hitter' means an assassin. 'dismissed' takes B out of the city's name and 'out' rearranges what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: A hired gun is someone paid to kill, a professional hit man.

clue.text: Dolls waiting in line to be delivered a meal?

indicators.note: words delivered are spoken, so this is how the phrase sounds

parts.note: Barbie dolls standing in a queue

explanation.surface: Toy dolls line up to have a meal brought to them.
explanation.walkthrough: Barbie is the toy doll and a queue is a line of people waiting.
explanation.definitionFit: A barbecue is an outdoor meal of food grilled over charcoal.

clue.text: Fighting dogs?

parts.note: a breed of dog shares its name with fighters in the ring

explanation.definitionFit: The breed of German dog shares its name with men who fight with their fists.

clue.text: See 20 down
'80s double act taken to extremes?

parts.note: a British comedy pair of the 1980s whose stage name names two opposite extremes of size

explanation.surface: A comedy duo of the 1980s pushed things too far.
explanation.walkthrough: Syd and Eddie were a British TV comedy double act, popular in the 1980s.
explanation.definitionFit: The duo's name pairs two opposite sizes, the two extremes from small to big.

clue.text: Over 90? Badly attired? Get state support!

indicators.note: the shuffled letters sit over the number, covering it on both sides
done badly, the letters of attired are put in a jumbled order

parts.note: taken as written
XC is 90 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Someone over ninety and badly dressed asks for state benefits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Badly' rearranges the letters into TAREDIT, and 'Over' wraps them round the Roman numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: A tax credit is a payment from the government, a form of state welfare support.

clue.text: No starter with fast food

indicators.note: with no starter, the word loses its first letter

parts.note: fast means firmly fixed, or stuck

explanation.surface: A meal without a first course, served with fast food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast food' reads as one phrase but 'fast' is the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuck is British school slang for food, especially sweets and snacks.

clue.text: Might he have starred in Carry On Up The Valley?

definitions.text: Might he have starred in Carry On Up The Valley?

parts.words: Might he have starred in Carry On Up The Valley?
parts.note: a regular actor in the British Carry On comedy films shares his surname with a word for a valley

explanation.walkthrough: The Carry On films were British comedies, among them Carry On Up the Khyber; Jim Dale starred in many.
explanation.definitionFit: Jim Dale was a Carry On actor, and a dale is a valley in northern England.

clue.text: See 15
Southern refined claret is a brilliant red

indicators.note: refining processes the wine, so its letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A refined claret from the south is a vivid red.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarlet is a bright, vivid shade of red.

clue.text: Exaggerated walk after 1/20th of a pint?

definitions.meaning: to stride off in an exaggerated, huffy manner
a British imperial pint is twenty fluid ounces, abbreviated fl oz

explanation.surface: A showy stroll after downing a small measure of drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To flounce is to move in an exaggerated, indignant way; a fl. ounce is a twentieth of an imperial pint.
